ANFIELD, LIVERPOOL — Dominik Szoboszlai believes he and Florian Wirtz have a special understanding on the field that can lift Liverpool to new heights. Andoni Iraola's Reds were rampant on Sunday as they took 10-man Manchester United to pieces with a 4-0 win at Anfield . Szoboszlai started the rout, hammering home the free-kick from the edge of the area that resulted from Leny Yoro's clumsy red-card challenge on Alexander Isak. Wirtz doubled Liverpool's advantage in the 13th minute with a clever volleyed finish from Rio Ngumoha's cross. It was the Germany playmaker's fifth goal in his past four games for club and country. MORE: Florian Wirtz primed for overdue Anfield moment as Liverpool host Pochettino's Man United The excellent Ngumoha got in on the act midway through the second half before Wirtz laid on the fourth goal for substitute Victor Munoz. Wirtz's relative lack of goal contributions since his £116.5million ($156m) move from Bayer Leverkusen last summer has prompted mounting criticism but he revelled against a beleaguered United in their first game under Mauricio Pochettino. “I always knew he's a good player. He's world-class," Szoboszlai said. "I love to play with him; we understand each other very well. “I think we are similar type of guys who understand the game in the same way. That's why it's easier for us. “Now he's in the flow, scoring against Crystal Palace , for the national team and scoring a goal today. item.title: Is Gent’s title challenge already begining to falter?
item.description: Is Gent’s title challenge already begining to falter? Rik De Mil will certainly not have enjoyed watching his Gent side this past weekend. Away to Beveren , the side lost 1-0 despite having a man advantage for the majority of the second-half. Arno Verscheuren was shown a red card just 10 minutes into the second half, but the Buffaloes were unable to make their superior numbers count. Instead, Gent saw Jearl Margaritha score the only goal of the game to help managerless Beveren to their first league win since the 12th of September. Gent, on the other hand, have won just two games in their last five in all competitions and are starting to see their title challenge falter somewhat. De Mil and his Gent side had started the season in fantastic form, and it probably shouldn’t be panic stations just yet. The defeat to Beveren was only their second of the league season, with the gap to Union St Gilloise now four points. That could become just one should Gent beat Union this coming weekend. However, the side have suffered from injuries to key players, including the former Union fan favourite Christian Burgess. While De Mil is known for playing attractive attacking football, it has been the defence that has shone for Gent this season, with just seven goals conceded in 12 games, the best defence alongside league leaders Union. After a European clash with FK Crvena Zvezda on Thursday, Gent will hope to get things back on track with a win over Union this weekend. With no play-offs and halving of points this season, if Gent have any aspirations of challenging for the league title they can ill afford to let the likes of Club Brugge or Union open up a decent lead on them this season, given how consistent both sides have been over the past few years. item.title: 49ers’ Nick Bosa bombarded by vulgar Spanish chants after shading Mexican fans
item.description: The fans in Mexico City were not ready to forgive Nick Bosa for comments made ahead of the San Francisco 49ers ‘ Sunday night showdown against the Minnesota Vikings at Estadio Azteca. Leading up to the game, Bosa made comments in the media that seemed to shade Mexican fans , going so far as to remark on their “soccer cheering” and saying, “some information given to the fans” so they know the appropriate time to cheer. Well, Mexican fans are going to cheer whenever they want, or they will heckle you. For Bosa, it was the latter on Sunday night. Bosa was booed mercilessly when he took the field at Estadio Azteca, but that was only the beginning. Throughout the night, Bosa was often met with chants of “culero” every time he was shown or involved in a play. In Mexican slang, culero translates roughly to “a**hole.” MORE: Nick Bosa’s girlfriend Ella Ailiff stuns in custom 49ers fit at Mexico City game amid controversy Nick Bosa Becomes Public Enemy No. 1 Culero chants for Nick Bosa! https://t.co/gDkUn9p2L4 — Gilberto Manzano (@GManzano24) November 23, 2026 Was that the appropriate time to break out a chant? Perhaps only Bosa will know. MORE: 49ers WAG Kristin Juszczyk ‘sidelined’ for Mexico City game but still repping team While Bosa was heckled throughout the game because of his comments, he and the 49ers got the last laugh. San Francisco steamrolled the Vikings, 35-10, proving once again why they are the current favorites to win the Super Bowl. item.title: Differing account of ‘gentleman’s agreement’ between Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala as plot thickens
item.description: (Photo by Harry Langer/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The latest reporting from Sky Germany’s Florian Plettenberg (via @iMiaSanMia ) adds another layer to the increasingly complicated discussion surrounding Jamal Musiala’s contract at Bayern Munich, particula rly when compared with the earlier report that Bayern believes a “gentleman’s agreement” with Musiala’s camp has been violated. According to Plettenberg, Uli Hoeneß met with Musiala’s agency at Tegernsee in August 2026. The meeting took place before Musiala’s condition was publicly disclosed and before his two collapses during the friendly matches against Leipzig and Heidenheim. Hoeneß was reportedly informed of Musiala’s health condition at the time, and the meeting was described as having taken place in a positive, trusting atmosphere. However, the crucial detail is what reportedly did not happen: no specific agre ements were reached regarding a potential contract adjustment if Musiala’s performan ces declined, and no assurances were made, either verbally or in writing. This new information appears to complicate the narrative outlined in the Süddeutsche Zeitung report that prompted our earlier coverage. That report claimed two legally non-binding gentlemen’s agreements were reached during a summer meeting between Hoeneß and Musiala’s agent, Christian Schmid — Bayern Munich would support Musiala through his recovery, and the contract could be adjusted in Bayern’s favor if Musiala continued to struggle with his health and medication side effects. The distinction between the two accounts is significant. The earlier report suggested an understanding existed regarding a possible contr actual adjustment if Musiala could not return to his previous level. Plettenberg’s reporting, however, expli citly denies that any such agreement, assurance, or commitment was made. That does not necessarily mean the two reports are entirely incomp atible. There could have been discussions about Musiala’s health, expectations, and the club’s concerns without eithe r party reaching a concrete understanding about modifying the contract. Even so, the latest reporting directly challenges the idea that Musiala’s camp agreed to a specific contingency involving his salary. Like every other aspect of this saga, we know some things, but not enough. For now, Bayern Munich’s frustration may be real, but the precise nature of any alleged gentleman’s agreement remains disputed—and that distinction matters enormously in this increasingly contentious saga. item.description: CHAMPAIGN, IL - NOVEMBER 21: Iowa Hawkeyes LB Jayden Montgomery (36) celebrating in the middle of a large group of players following college football game between the Iowa Hawkeyes and Illinois Fighting Illini on November 21, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Just keep winning. It sounds overly simplistic, like there should be a deeper strategy behind what it takes to separate yourself in the Big Ten standings, and how you stack up against the national competition. But it’s been Kirk Ferentz’s mantra for decades now, and especially as of late during his weekly pressers. And I am willing to bet it was what was on the player’s minds when they took the field for the second half on Saturday versus Illinois. Saturday was the fifth time this season that Iowa has not allowed their opponent to score a single point in the second half. And on what looked to be a relatively quiet weekend for B1G matchups, chaos erupted. Undefeated UCLA lost at Michigan, Indiana lost at Washington, OSU was upset at Nebraska, and even Rutgers won at Penn State. Let’s take pause and look at the B1G conference standings. UCLA is on top at 7-1. Indiana, Oregon, and Iowa are now tied at 6-2 for second place. With Wisconsin, USC, and Ohio State all tied for third place at 5-3. Four more teams are tied for fourth place at 4-4. Fourteen teams in the Big Ten are now bowl eligible. So how is Iowa different this year? This game against Illinois was a microcosm of what this season has held. The Variety of Receivers Catching Passes Six different players had receptions on Saturday, and that’s actually on the low end for this season. More commonly, it’s seven or eight different players. And on Saturday, the top two receivers, in terms of total catches and yardage, were wide receivers Tony Diaz annd Reece Vander Zee versus tight ends. While we’re on the topic, I will call out that it is good to see tight end Thomas Meyer getting involved and making catches as the season progresses, as Iowa will need him next year after Addison Ostrenga and Zach Ortwerth graduate. The Variety of Play Calls & Weapons No longer is Iowa predictable, and the variety of players able to make a reception or rush for an end around sweep keeps defenses guessing when players like Diaz, Reece Vander Zee, or DJ Vonnahme go in motion. Now the wrinkle of Hank Brown getting the call for designed quarterback runs adds to the unpredictability. Perhaps none more notable when Iowa had fourth and goal at the 2-yard line, and chose to run a QB keeper with Brown for the touchdown to cap their infamous 91-yard drive that consumed over ten minutes in the third and fourth quarters to put Iowa up by 27-17. item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - OCTOBER 14: Andrew Vaughn #28 of the Milwaukee Brewers greets teammates prior to Game Three of the National League Championship Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday, October 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Welcome back to our look around the Brewers’ roster at potential targets that could help the team! As detailed in our introduction , there’s not a ton of wiggle room in the Brewers’ infield, except for one notable exception. That exception is at first base, where we see the one place on the roster that a big hole was taken out of the 2026 World Series-winning club after Jake Bauers left for Boston in free agency. Before we get to that, let’s quickly recap where things sit at the other infield positions, where things look to be set for the forseeable future. Brice Turang, one of the best players in the league, is locked in at second base and is under team control through 2029. Cooper Pratt, at shortstop, is under team control through 2033 with two additional club options. Unless a trade happens (not out of the question!), Milwaukee will almost certainly start the season with a platoon of Joey Ortiz and David Hamilton at third base; both players are arbitration-eligible for the first time in 2026, and, like Turang, would hit free agency after the 2029 season. Of course, no one is under any illusions that this infield will look like it does right now for the next three years even if everyone is under contract, and that’s because one of the game’s top prospects, Jesús Made, is coming. Made played the entire 2026 season at Double-A Biloxi and it seems likely that he’ll start the 2026 season at Triple-A Nashville. But Made’s career has, in many ways, mirrored Jackson Chourio’s, and when Chourio was at the same point in his career, he signed a 10-year contract and was on the Opening Day roster. The Brewers are surely thinking about offering a similar type of contract to Made, if they haven’t already, and if he accepts, it’s not out of the question that he could start the year in the majors—especially if the start of the season is delayed due to the lockout. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 23: Randy Arozarena #56 of the Seattle Mariners reacts after hitting a single during the fifth inning against the Houston Astros at T-Mobile Park on September 23, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the last few years, the Yankees have entered every single winter needing to add at least one outfielder. Following the disastrous 2023 season, where Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Billy McKinney, and Franchy Cordero combined for 141 games (and that’s just three of the many disastrous outfielders rotated through that season), the team rebuilt just about their entire outfield corps in two days by swinging deals for Trent Grisham, Alex Verdugo, and Juan Soto. With the departure of the latter two in free agency, the team traded for Cody Bellinger the following year, and with both Grisham and Bellinger free agents after last season, the team’s No. 1 priority last winter was to keep the band together. This year, that has changed. Aaron Judge and Bellinger are under contract for the foreseeable future, Grisham is a goner, Spencer Jones acquitted himself well in 86 games, and despite his troubles in 2026, the Yankees don’t appear to have completely given up on former top prospect Jasson Domínguez. And let’s not forget Heliot Ramos, who is currently slated to serve as a platoon bench bat. That being said, the team desperately needs to add some right-handed bats this winter. While the Yankees did, technically, hit better against lefties than righties this past year — a 105 wRC+ against southpaws, compared to 100 against righties — the lineup leaned left-handed dominant last season. And so, although third base and the bullpen are undoubtedly the Yankees’ priorities this winter, they have been doing their due diligence, checking in on a number of right-handed bats. item.title: Jets Watch: Utah’s Power Play Could Expose One of Winnipeg’s Biggest Weaknesses
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets have earned points in eight of their past nine games, but Monday’s matchup against the Utah Mammoth could test one of their biggest weaknesses. Utah has one of the NHL’s most dangerous power plays, while the Jets have struggled to kill penalties. If the Jets spend too much time shorthanded, their recent improvement at even strength might not be enough. item.description: Looking back on it 40 years later, you miss the tuxedos for the occasion. The HBO broadcast crew of Barry Tompkins, “Sugar” Ray Leonard and Larry Merchant, in their finest evening dress, dapper down to the cufflinks, gathered at the Las Vegas Hilton for what Merchant called a “coronation more than a contest.” On Nov. 22, 1986, Mike Tyson, just 20 years and four months old, was set to become boxing’s youngest ever heavyweight world champion. It felt like a chandelier affair, even if, as Tompkins points out, it was in fact the “diametric opposite.” Tyson, a kid from the Brooklyn who’d been taken under wing by Cus D’Amato, stalked toward the boxing ring for his title bout with Trevor Berbick wearing his trademark white towel as a shirt, crudely slit down the middle to slip over his head. He was in the iconic black trunks, which would earn him a $5,000 fine for insubordination because Berbick had elected to wear black, and Mike wasn’t yet the champion. The heightened sense of anticipation belonged to that word: Yet . Invincibility is a fool’s notion, after all, while inevitability is straight terror. Even at 20 years old — especially at 20 — Tyson brokered in the kind of doom that could do 50 shares for HBO, which means that 50% of all households with HBO would tune in. He dealt in the kind of doom that didn’t belong to the tamer confines of sport, but to a savagery that instead delved deeper into man’s innermost darkness. Fighting from the shell, he would hold his palms at his chin and nuzzle into his opponent, only to explode from the inside with an uppercut or right hook, from his legs through the knuckle, and from the cruelest of angles, to snap a man’s head back from his shoulders. Mike Tyson (L) had 15 fights in his debut year as a professional, winning all by knockout. Andy Hayt via Getty Images Everyone knew Berbick, the WBC heavyweight champion heading into what was being billed as the Heavyweight World Series, was in well over his head. item.title: The Toronto Maple Leafs’ Collapse Started Years Ago. Firing Jim Hiller Won’t Fix It.
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Toronto Maple Leafs have spent much of the past decade trying to figure out why a team with so much talent has accomplished so little when it matters most. Coaches have come and gone, executives have been replaced, and the roster has undergone significant changes. Yet somehow, the Leafs keep finding themselves back in the same conversation. Now, with another miserable stretch of hockey putting the organization under the microscope, the question is once again what needs to change. But there’s something worth considering before the Leafs decide who deserves the blame this time. What if their problems aren’t nearly as new as they appear? A look through the past 10 seasons of the Leafs’ underlying numbers suggests they’ve been moving in the wrong direction for years. And for a while, their results were good enough to hide it. The Maple Leafs Have Been Losing Ground for Years During the 2021-22 season, the Leafs were one of the NHL’s strongest teams at 5-on-5. According to Natural Stat Trick, they controlled 55.24% of expected goals. That’s an excellent number over an 82-game season. The Leafs scored 208 goals and allowed 182 at 5-on-5, and there was plenty of reason to believe they could compete with just about anybody. The problem is that the Leafs haven’t been able to sustain that level of play. Their 5-on-5 expected-goals share dropped to 53.54% in 2022-23, then 51.54% in 2023-24. By 2024-25, they were down to 48.52%, meaning opponents were generating better scoring chances over the course of the season. It wasn’t a sudden collapse. Their share of expected goals declined for four consecutive seasons, eventually reaching 45.67% in 2025-26. And while the changes behind the bench and in the front office understandably attracted attention, the numbers suggest the decline was already underway. The Maple Leafs’ Success in 2024-25 Hid a Serious Problem During the 2024-25 season, the Leafs scored 169 goals and allowed just 136 at 5-on-5. That’s a goal differential of plus-33, and they accounted for 55.41% of the goals scored when the teams were playing at even strength. Those are the kinds of numbers you’d expect from a team controlling games, except the Leafs weren’t. They generated 159.04 expected goals and allowed 168.75, giving them a negative expected-goals differential of 9.71. They were being outchanced in terms of quality, yet finished the season outscoring opponents by 33 goals. That’s a swing of more than 42 goals between their actual differential and what their expected-goals numbers suggested. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 28: Jake Bauers #9 of the Milwaukee Brewers poses for a photo with The Commissioner's Trophy in the clubhouse following Game Five of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The votes are in for our No. 5 spot in this year’s MVBrewers rankings, and it’s a former Brewer in the form of first baseman Jake Bauers. Bauers, who signed with the Red Sox just over a week ago, garnered 65 of the 106 total votes (61.3%), easily beating Aaron Ashby (31 votes), Trevor Megill (five votes), Garrett Mitchell (three votes), Abner Uribe (one vote), and Sal Frelick (one write-in vote from @mlv234). Bauers, now 31, is coming off what was easily the best season of his career. After totaling negative WAR over the first six seasons of his career with the Rays, Indians (Guardians), Mariners, Yankees, and Brewers, he played in a career-high 144 games in 2026, hitting .266/.389/.484 with a team-high 26 homers, 22 doubles, 86 RBIs, 93 runs, and 11 steals. His 140 OPS+ was also far and away the best of his career, outpacing the 111 mark he put up in 2025. While he was slightly below average defensively, he served as a key cog in Pat Murphy’s lineups, earning a Silver Slugger at the utility position. His ability to draw walks was particularly elite, as he had a 16.3% walk rate, ranking in the 98th percentile. He also ranked in the top 10% in xwOBA (.371), average exit velocity (92.1 mph), barrel rate (14.0%), hard-hit rate (51.9%), launch angle sweet-spot rate (38.6%), bat speed (76.5 mph), and chase rate (21.7%). In the postseason, Bauers continued to draw walks, even as he struggled to collect hits in the World Series. He finished the playoffs hitting .191/.345/.277 with a homer, a double, six RBIs, four runs, and 10 walks. He was especially good in the NLCS, earning MVP honors as he hit .286/.412/.571 with both of those extra-base hits, all six RBIs, and three walks. As with just about every other player on the Brewers, Bauers had a signature moment in the postseason — in fact, he had two. First, it was a huge 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in NLCS Game 2 , loading the bases for Christian Yelich, who promptly singled a pair home to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead. 2026 PitchingNinja Award for At Bat of the Year ending in a Walk. 🏆 Winner: Jake Bauers' Epic 12 Pitch Walk pic.twitter.com/eSD7G5HlPP — Rob Friedman (@PitchingNinja) November 21, 2026 Just two days later, it was Bauers facing off with Blake Snell in the seventh inning of NLCS Game 3 . This time, Bauers saw 11 pitches, and on that 11th pitch, he slugged a huge two-run homer, flipping the scoreboard to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead they wouldn’t relinquish. 2026 PitchingNinja Award for At Bat of the Year ending in a Home Run. 🏆 Winner: Jake Bauers' Epic 11 Pitch AB HR.

item.description: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something in the water when it comes to wide receivers in Pittsburgh that turns them into clowns. It’s been this way since the halcyon days of Hines Ward, as the team has managed, time and time and time again, to be saddled with problematic guys and know exactly when to part ways before the ticking time bomb explodes. Until DK Metcalf arrived. This is the organization’s big mistake, the whiff that is setting them back, and Sunday was a perfect example of how much of a disaster Metcalf has been for this team. It isn’t simply about losing to a hopeless Eagles team, or Metcalf getting ejected for poking Cooper DeJean in the eye , or even losing pace in the AFC North — it’s all of these things in concert, and the fact that they’re paying through the moon for this guy to actively hurt their team. Perhaps the worst part of all this is that anyone could see this was a HORRIBLE move for the Steelers when they made it. Receivers are mercurial. No position in sports is more based on vibes and emotions than WR, and the second a receiver loses their confidence or stops getting fed, the majority will pitch a fit like an ornery toddler you forgot to bring snacks for. Metcalf was a reliable 1,000-yard guy in Seattle because of how he played the game. The Seahawks established everything through their run game, then used Metcalf to generate explosive plays downfield. This is why he averaged over 15 yards per catch downfield and had a reputation as the best deep ball guy in the NFL. What a receiver with a penchant for deep throws shouldn’t fool anyone: Deep throws. *Gasp*, I know it’s a shocker — but you kind of need a guy with a big enough arm to stretch the field to get the best out of Metcalf’s skillset. Know what old-man Aaron Rodgers doesn’t have? A big arm. At no point during any of his career was Rodgers an elite deep passer. He was always known for his intelligence on intermediate routes and an incredible ability to find the open man when operating out of structure. There was never a chance Metcalf was going to be a good fit for this iteration of the Steelers, and it’s been a wreck. Metcalf had a career-low 59 receptions in 2025, for a career-low 850 yards. item.title: New number, new position, new coaches. Same Groot, bigger results.
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins is sacked by Greg Rousseau #15 of the Buffalo Bills for an 8-yard loss during the first quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has reinvented himself this year. A new position, a new number, new coaches and an entirely new defensive scheme. And the results? Is it too early to start throwing around the word legendary ? Maybe, but Rousseau is certainly making a case for it. With two sacks against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Rousseau has officially entered uncharted territory in his NFL career. His 10 sacks this season are a new personal best. Greg Rousseau is up to 9 sacks on the year, establishing a new career-high and marking the most sacks by a Bill in the first 10 games of a season since Lorenzo Alexander (10 sacks) in 2016. pic.twitter.com/4ZHZAZirZj — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 22, 2026 Rousseau sacked Miami quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss that forced the Dolphins to punt after a five-play first drive. Then in the second quarter, it was an almost identical play. Rousseau dropped McCord for another eight-yard loss. Greg Rousseau is now up to 10 sacks on the season. Today marks Rousseau’s fourth game of the year with 2+ sacks, the most multi-sack games by any player in the NFL this season. pic.twitter.com/gnKnwxEDCH — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 22, 2026 Rousseau entered the NFL in 2021 as a defensive end, spending his first five seasons in Sean McDermott’s defensive system. Along the way, he worked under Leslie Frazier, McDermott himself, and Bobby Babich as defensive leaders, while learning from defensive line coaches Eric Washington and Marcus West. Then came 2026, and just about everything changed. Jim Leonhard took over as defensive coordinator, bringing a new scheme that moved Rousseau from defensive end to outside linebacker. Bobby April III became his new position coach, giving Rousseau his third position coach and fourth defensive leader in six NFL seasons. Somehow, through all that change, Rousseau is putting together the most productive season of his career. He recorded four sacks as a rookie in 2021, eight in 2022, five in 2023, eight again in 2024 and seven last season. Those eight-sack performances had been his personal best until Sunday. Of course, Rousseau didn’t exactly ease into his new role — he came roaring in right from the start. He opened the season with three consecutive two-sack games, becoming the first player in Bills history to accomplish that feat. Only two other players in NFL history had ever done it. For a player who spent the offseason learning a different position in a new defense, the transition has looked remarkably smooth. With seven games remaining, Rousseau has already accomplished something he hadn’t managed in any of his previous five seasons.

The Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors took on the Boston Celtics during their recent game in the NBA season. In a low-scoring 88-87 win, veteran forward Draymond Green became the hero of the game by playing suffocating defence against the Celtics’ Jayson Tatum during the final possession of the game. Draymond Green explains his plan against Jayson Tatum With the shot clock running down, the Celtics handed the ball to Tatum, who tried to get free and nail a game-winning two-pointer. However, Green kept him in check, and while Tatum got the shot off in time, it hit the rim and fell out as the Warriors snapped their five-game losing streak. Green spoke about the moment during his post-game interview, stating: “I wanted him to go left. A little better odds when he’s going left than right. But he’s a great player.” “So great players are going to get to where they’re trying to go on the floor. He was trying to go right, and I just knew I couldn’t let him go all the way to the rim. “Make him take a contested two, if he makes it, he’s Jayson Tatum, he makes them for a reason; I’ll live with the results,” Green added. While Green couldn’t push Tatum to the left side, he still disrupted his flow enough to alter the path, which led to the Celtics star missing the game-winner. But at no point did Green think that he had the upper hand over a player of JT’s caliber on the offensive end of the floor. On a different night, the shot may have fallen, and the Celtics would have walked away with a win, but this time, fortune favoured Green. item.description: Josh Allen's Bills teammate just accomplished something LaDainian Tomlinson never did originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Josh Allen has become the face of the Buffalo Bills , but one of his teammates is putting together a historic season that deserves considerably more national attention. James Cook continued his remarkable rushing streak Sunday during Buffalo's 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins , gaining 89 yards and scoring a touchdown. The performance extended Cook's streak of games with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown to nine. That's a number that places him alongside some of the greatest running backs in NFL history. Cook surpassed the single-season marks of LaDainian Tomlinson and John Riggins, who each accomplished the feat in eight consecutive games.Only Terry Allen has recorded a longer such streak across games spanning multiple seasons, reaching 10 consecutive games with Washington from 1995 to 1996. For Cook, the accomplishment reflects a level of week-to-week consistency that few running backs have maintained. James Cook breaks impressive NFL rushing record Cook carried the football 22 times for 89 yards against Miami, scoring on a one-yard run during the second quarter. The touchdown was his 10th rushing score of the season and his ninth consecutive game reaching the end zone on the ground. It also established a Bills franchise record for consecutive games with a rushing touchdown. Cook's production has become a defining part of Buffalo's offensive identity. Allen remains one of the NFL's most dangerous dual-threat quarterbacks, but Cook gives the Bills a dependable rushing option capable of keeping defenses from focusing exclusively on the passing game. The two have also accomplished something unprecedented together. According to the Bills, Cook and Allen are the first pair of NFL teammates to record at least 10 rushing touchdowns apiece in three consecutive seasons. That's a remarkable achievement considering how rarely quarterbacks and running backs both produce double-digit rushing touchdown totals. Allen's mobility creates opportunities near the goal line, while Cook's vision and consistency have made him increasingly valuable. MORE : C.J. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter.
